content: The surest way to corrupt a youth is to instruct him to hold in higher esteem those who think alike than those who think differently.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. From childhood, we are trained to fit in, to smooth over our eccentricities, and to mirror the expectations of those around us. But copying others only buys superficial acceptance at the cost of your own soul.

In Friedrich Nietzsche's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Your unique perspective and lived contradictions are your greatest offering to the world. The moment you stop performing and stand firmly in your own skin, you command an authority that imitation can never manufacture.
reflectionPrompt: Where in your current routine are you choosing convenient illusion over uncomfortable truth?
